reader_flags.reason: Benign red-marrow foci do not supply a whole-bone injury assessment.

Croatian obostrano interpreted as both compartments within one continuous knee report; no separate left/right examination sections. Larger Baker and moderate fluid qualify. Cartilage extent remains missing.
ACL partial anteromedial tear fraction unknown; bare cartilage grade II does not specify grading convention.
PF cartilage loss reaches 50% without exceeding it, below strict threshold. Discoid meniscus is a variant without tear.
Explicit no cartilage loss retained for FT targets despite mild-to-moderate thinning/fraying. Qualified subchondral-bone statement not a whole-injury exclusion.
Normal-thickness plica is not an assessment of the entire synovial lining.
Body no-synovitis conflicts with final diffuse-synovitis diagnosis; uncertain. Medial tear suggested, lateral meniscus unmentioned. Exact source newline preserved in PF quote.
Considerable Greek fluid interpreted qualifying volume. PF fissure-like erosions/fraying not explicitly shallow. Lateral named ICRS II plus superficial qualifier supports negative.
Only global no-abnormality summary, no named target assessment; all targets unmentioned.
Continuous ACL with prior partial tear versus strain lacks current fraction/status. Bare lateral I and PF II uncalibrated.
Medial bare grade III degeneration/extrusion not direct tear. Widespread fluid describes distribution without volume. Grade I MCL negative; direct synovitis positive.
Corrupted cartilage heading provides no informative cartilage assessment. Patellar retinacular-attachment marrow edema nonspecific.
Explicit left-knee report; both-sided menisci interpreted its two menisci, not a combined bilateral examination.
Explicit no acute fracture/bruise retained despite reactive lateral edema and benign bone island. Lateral high-grade fissure extent missing.
Normal PF template conflicts with multiple defects and final bare grade4; uncertain. Explicit no acute fracture/bruise retained despite patellar edema.

Complete ACL and both direct meniscal tears; extensive hemarthrosis positive. Definite avulsion fragments with hemorrhage suggest recent injury, but explicit acute timing absent, fracture retained uncertain. Medial capsular avulsion does not name MCL.
Explicit minor cartilage fraying/no loss below threshold despite conclusion mentioning mild thinning.
Direct tibial bone contusion positive/no fracture. Normal popliteal fossa supports Baker absence; separate vastus-medialis ganglion excluded from that target.
Normal lateral compartment interpreted as normal meniscus and cartilage; scope flag. Direct synovitis positive, small effusion below threshold.
Possible ACL partial tear versus mucoid change. General cartilage wear with focal PF bare3-4 lacks depth/extent. Bone island and reactive cysts are not whole-bone injury exclusions.
Normal remaining marrow signal does not resolve nonspecific focal medial tibial edema or acute-fracture status.

Chronic ACL rupture with proximal discontinuity and partial horizontalization lacks explicit complete/high-grade fraction; uncertain. Named ICRSIII depth known, extent missing. Direct mild bone bruise positive, fracture uncertain.
Hoffa fat-pad impingement alone supplies no target-level assessment.
Bare PF gradeIV/thinning and 1cm anterior lateral femoral OC lesion do not establish depth/qualified extent or exact FT versus trochlear surface. FT osteophytes do not grade cartilage.
Full-thickness loss on both medial surfaces lacks region extent; marginal lateral OA ungraded.
Normal marrow signal supports contusion negative but does not explicitly assess fracture morphology.
Explicit shallow PF fissures below threshold independent of bare grade2. Normal bone signal without morphology leaves fracture uncertain.
Anterior lateral femoral minor thinning lacks depth and exact FT-versus-trochlear correspondence; lateral/PF masked. Qualified no sinister bone changes not full injury exclusion.
Medial tear suggested; discoid lateral variant with no categorical tear criteria retained negative. Qualified normal marrow not complete fracture/contusion exclusion.

Weightbearing higher-grade cartilage reduction lacks exact compartment/depth; PF mixed partly-full loss lacks qualifying-region extent. Small hemarthrosis negative; numeric-only 4.5cm Baker ungraded. Plica alone not synovitis.

General normal cartilage interpreted all compartments; normal lateral compartment includes meniscus. Insufficiency microtrabecular fracture/edema without collapse lacks acute timing/discrete line evidence.
Explicit no contusion only; fracture unmentioned. Extra-articular muscular nodule does not supply target evidence.
Avascular necrosis not explicit bone contusion or acute-fracture assessment. Leaking Baker does not establish volume grade.

Near-complete denudation of medial femoral/tibial cartilage supplies qualitative extent and depth. Extensive fluid interpreted qualifying. Synovial proliferation alone uncertain; numeric-only small dimensions do not grade Baker.
Patellar cortical irregularity adjacent loose body lacks acute timing and contusion assessment.
Lateral patellar loss explicitly >50% but extent missing; medial loss does not exceed50%. Parameniscal/pes collections not Baker.
Probable enchondromatous tibial lesions without cortical destruction plus remaining bones normal form/signal interpreted nontraumatic/no acute fracture; scope flag.
Lateral direct horizontal tear overrides accompanying bare gradeIII degeneration; bone signal normal only leaves fracture morphology uncertain.
Mild/moderate chondropathy uncalibrated. Explicit no fractures retained despite chronic tibial tuberosity ossicle.
Lateral described as degenerative tear positive. Named PF ICRSIV depth known but extent absent; 6mm loose body is not cartilage-loss size.

Final direct medial tear resolves earlier suspicion; lateral remains rule-out. Final explicitly large Baker qualifies independent of numeric8cm. MCL normal-template versus grade1 does not change below-threshold result.
Menisci unmentioned. Normal surrounding soft tissue not a specific Baker or synovitis assessment.
Normal marrow signal supports contusion negative; patella alone structurally normal does not exclude all acute fractures.

Explicit chronic complete ACL positive; borderline discoid lateral variant not a tear. Small Baker and fluid negative; synovial-cyst terminology not synovitis. Marrow normal alone leaves fracture uncertain.

notes: Personally read all50 original gold-blinded reports in five groups of ten and reasoned all600 targets under frozen rubric. No other051 annotations, gold, legacy/external labels, regex/NLI labeling or default filling accessed/used. Python only assembled explicit personal choices and validated exact contiguous original-language quotes, schema and UID coverage through rsna.labels.read_reviews. Unfinished work stayed outside initiative. Explicit absence and below-threshold findings distinguished in notes; missing severity/extent/acuity/anatomy and contradictions masked. Only completion/coverage/hashes shared with root; flags withheld pending independent source-first review. Draft does not confer training eligibility or image diagnostic accuracy.
